subject: Private fleet maintenance: cross-site upgrade window & undo-path rehearsal
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private fleet maintenance: initial window proposal and runbook ask

Team —

Following our kickoff yesterday, proposing an initial maintenance window for Greenline Bank’s private deployment: Saturday 2028-05-18 02:00–06:00 UTC (narrow window to align with Greenline change control). The goal: apply the 2.3.1 runtime patch (security + kv-cache eviction fix), bump model-serving runtime from v12.7 -> v12.9, and apply the network ACL tweaks they requested.

Asks:
- Karthik: can you outline the canary slices and the one-hour rollback verification steps (I want specific health endpoints and expected metrics)?
- Naomi: coordinate with NetOps on BGP route hold/propagation timing and confirm whether we need a pre-maintenance AS-path announce to avoid mid-window flaps.
- Soojin: please prepare the snapshot checklist and DB migration dry-run notes (even if there are no schema changes, we need TPS/latency baselines).

Attached: maintenance-notice.pdf (customer-facing window proposal). I’ll draft the external approval email after we confirm rollback criteria.

Mina
Principal PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private fleet maintenance: initial window proposal and runbook ask

Mina — thanks. High-level plan below, I’ll drop a runbook snippet into the Drive folder. Short answers up-front: canary = 10% of nodes (control-plane + 1 replica each region), full cutoff at 60%. Rollback timeframe target = 30 min from trigger to traffic-stable on previous version.

Canary plan (details to be added to runbook):
- Preflight (T-3h): healthchecks, KV cache warmup baseline, snapshot verification.
- Canary slice (T+0 to T+20 min): update 10% of nodes with v12.9, keep routing to old model for inference (traffic-split 90/10). Monitor: 200-level success, tokens-per-second, p95 latency on generate endpoint, kv-cache hit rate.
- Observation (T+20 to T+40): if no regressions, ramp to 30% then 60% (T+40 to T+80).

Rollback triggers (examples):
- sustained p95 latency > 500ms over 5 minutes (baseline currently 210ms)
- error rate > 1% for token generation requests
- client-facing 5xx or model mismatch regressions detected by evals (automated golden-set check fails)

Rollback mechanics:
1) Toggle routing policy to previous model variant (feature-flag flip) — this restores inference traffic in <60s.
2) If node-level issues present (kernel panic / driver-level crash), use snapshot rollback: revert instance from pre-maintenance image (expected time: 12–25 mins depending on attach speed).
3) Post-rollback verification: run synthetic golden-set and confirm kv-cache hit-rate back to baseline.

Network considerations: we should avoid BGP withdraws during the ramp. Naomi, if we need to quiesce a peering, prefer announcing a de-preferred path rather than withdrawal.

I’ll add the exact CURL checks and Grafana panels to the runbook.

— Karthik
Senior SRE, Inference Runtime
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@greenlinebank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@greenlinebank.com
Date: Sun, 6 May 2028 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private fleet maintenance: initial window proposal and runbook ask

Hi Mina —

Thanks for the proposed window. Greenline can provision the change control for 2028-05-18 02:00–06:00 UTC but we need:
1) A short, non-technical summary for our ops managers (one paragraph)
2) Confirmation of the rollback SLA (how quickly you can restore service)
3) A list of IPs/prefixes that will change, and whether we will see any BGP withdraws so we can schedule with our firewall team.

Please include the maintenance-notice.pdf as part of the packet. We must receive final runbook and snapshot checklist by EOD 2028-05-10 to approve.

Ellen
Director, Platform Ops
Greenline Bank

Attachment: acceptance-template.docx (stub)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@greenlinebank.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 May 2028 13:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private fleet maintenance: network plan and IPs for Greenline change control

Ellen —

Quick network notes to include in the packet:
- No BGP withdraws will be executed during the ramp. We will perform AS-path de-preference by announcing a lower-priority community to our upstreams for any nodes we want to isolate (see network-acl-diff.txt attached).
- Expected visible changes to Greenline: new IPs for the v12.9 control-plane endpoints (two /32s per-region). We will provide the full list 72 hours before the window.
- We will not change your public-facing VIPs; NAT translation will be preserved.

Rollback-specific items:
- If the routing toggle fails to stabilize, we will trigger image restore using pre-maintenance snapshots (snapshot-checklist.md attached). Estimated time to restore traffic to previous image: 12–25 minutes depending on block-storage attach time.
- Our runbook contains an emergency-evacuate command that locks new traffic and drains active sessions gracefully (we will provide the exact kubectl/drain sequence).

Naomi Feldman
Network Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: network-acl-diff.txt, snapshot-checklist.md
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@greenlinebank.com>, ops@greenlinebank.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 May 2028 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private fleet maintenance: cross-site upgrade window & undo-path rehearsal — final packet planned

Thanks, Ellen — confirming we’ll provide:
- Non-technical summary (one paragraph) for your ops packet (attached to the Drive link).
- Rollback SLA: we guarantee a traffic restoration method (feature-flag routing flip) within 60s for control-plane routing; full image-based restore within 25 minutes worst-case. We will record timestamps in the change ticket for audit.
- IP/prefix list: will be delivered T-72h (2028-05-15 02:00 UTC).
- Final runbook + snapshot checklist delivered by EOD 2028-05-10 per your request.

Operational notes for Greenline ops team (short):
1) No public VIP changes; only control-plane endpoints will have new ephemeral IPs.
2) We will use AS-path de-preference rather than withdraws to avoid transient route loss.
3) If you see >30s of control-plane wobble after routing flip, please open severity-2 with our on-call and follow the runbook step: "Lock traffic + snapshot-restore".

I’ll upload the final runbook and attach the maintenance-notice.pdf + network-acl-diff and snapshot-checklist to the shared Drive folder and link the Jira ticket. Looking to close approvals by May 10.

Mina
Principal PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
